ACTIVATE
Author: Command Master

Type: Command

Syntax: activate <item>|<inv slot> [target] [room|inv|eq]

entries.title: ANTHIAN
entries.body:
ANTHIAN
Type: Race
Keywords: Anthian
Genders: Male, Female, Non-Binary
Allowed Classes: Fighter, Cleric: Order of the Heart, Cleric: Order of the Sword, Cleric:
Order of the Hand, Bard, Thief, Barbarian, Forester, Rune Mage
Racial Tensions: They form their own opinions of each race as they play
Racial Abilities: None

Anthians are short humanoids with bird and reptilian-like features, distinguished by their
feathered wings which grant them the gift of natural flight. Males range from 4'0" to 5'2"
in height, while females span 3'7" to 4'8". They possess sharp facial characteristics and
are renowned for their exceptionally beautiful singing voices, which resemble melodic bird
chirping.

Their lightweight physiology, while enabling flight, restricts their cargo capacity and
physical strength compared to larger races. Anthians embrace a reclusive lifestyle,
establishing small communities in natural terrain rather than urban centers. They gravitate
toward canyons, bluffs and cliffs, crags and rocky outcroppings. They share cultural
parallels with Leuians, prioritizing family bonds, community loyalty, and heritage pride.

Bards represent their most frequent urban role, leveraging their vocal talents. Foresters
also align well with their nature-oriented culture. Anthians traditionally favor Elindale
as their primary deity but may follow any religious path and alignment.

To learn more about the Anthian please visit the web page:
http://dragonsgatereborn.com/races/race-anthian.html


See: help <ability name>, help <class name>, help races

entries.title: ARACHNIAN
entries.body:
ARACHNIAN
Type: Race
Keywords: Arachnian
Genders: Male, Female, Non-Binary
Allowed Classes: Fighter, Cleric: Order of the Heart, Cleric: Order of the Sword, Cleric:
Order of the Hand, Thief, Barbarian
Racial Tensions: Penthanian, Secian
Racial Abilities: None

Arachnians are highly intelligent spider-like beings who inhabit the Great Waste in
northern Spur's continent, ruled by the fearsome Matriarch. An ancient conflict with the
Penthanians resulted in the loss of their rune-magick abilities when Penthanian mages
unleashed UnMagick, transforming the Arachnians into chaotic, hostile beings. They are
cruel and aggressive, displaying single-mindedly biased attitudes toward other races,
particularly despising Penthanians and viewing Secians as embodying their lost magical
abilities. Some legends suggest they were originally followers of Order, and prophecies
foretell the restoration of their lost powers. Arachnians possess natural body armor in the
form of a tough carapace, night vision, high resistance to destructive magic, exceptional
strength and dexterity, and the ability to throw webs and deliver fanged bites. They are
known for their advanced understanding of alchemy theory.

To learn more about the Arachnian please visit the web page:
http://dragonsgatereborn.com/races/race-arachnian.html


See: help <ability name>, help <class name>, help races

Author: Command Master
Keywords: call pets animal tag mounts
Type: Command

Syntax: call <item> - summons the pet on a pet tag or mount on a mount tag!
Syntax: call <slot> - summons the pet on a pet tag or mount on a mount tag!
Syntax: call patreonPet - summons the patreon pet, if one is made. Use the Patreon command to create a pet!
Syntax: call patreonMount - summons and mounts the patreon mount, if one is made. Use the Patreon command to create a mount! (Tier 5)

The call command summons a mount, a new pet, dismisses a pet, or returns a lost pet to your
side.

Typically, pets and mounts must be purchased or acquired through a role play event. They
can then be summoned with the call command and controlled with the order command.

Pets can perish and be lost forever. Be careful of giving them rare and expensive items as
they can be easily lost as pet inventory is not saved. Mounts do not perish and last
forever.

entries.title: COLOR
entries.body:
COLOR
Author: Command Master
Keywords: color colorset ansi colors colours
Type: Command

Syntax: color set <type> <colorTag>|default - sets the given type to use the indicated color tag.
Syntax: color list - lists all current colors.

Syntax: color brief - toggles brief color on/off.
Syntax: color none - toggles no color on/off.
Syntax: color xterm - toggles xterm color(256 colors - need client support) on/off.
Syntax: color trueColor - toggles true color on/off and xterm on if off.


The color command can change many aspects of color in A Tempest Season.

The following color codes exist:
#c/#C: cyan/bright cyan
#r/#R: red/bright red
#g/#G: green/bright green
#b/#B: blue/bright blue
#p/#P: purple/bright purple
#y/#Y: yellow/bright yellow
#s/#S: gray/black
#w/#W: gray/white
#d: default color
#h: default highlight color
#x: terminates color and reverts to client's default


The game also supports xterm color (type: color xterm to turn on):
#e1 to #e255: a specific color, that matches the chart from the following website:
https://i.stack.imgur.com/KTSQa.png

The game also supports true color (type: color trueColor to turn on):
#t(6-digit hex code): a specific color that matches the hex code in rgb color space. Example: #t(e3cdb6)
#t[keyword]: a specific color that matches the keyword. Example: #t[cotton]
 Note: Keywords are added by Actinate and Dayrinni. Not all keywords will exist.

See: help put, help get, help look,

The combat timer begins whenever a hostile action is performed. Certain commands and
actions are restricted while in a combat timer, such as the quit command.

The delays tick down every second and any commands entered which also are delayed, will be
placed in the queue. Not all commands are delayed actions, and can be performed while in
delay. Commands like say, inventory, and skills are examples for non-delayed commands.

entries.title: DESCRIPTION
entries.body:
DESCRIPTION
Author: Command Master
Keywords: description 
Type: Command

Syntax: description - enters the editor to write a description about your character..


The description command enters editing mode to write the description(physical and
background) for what players see when they look at you. The description text displays
immediately when a player looks at you - at the very top. The numbered lines in the
description editor do not display when a player looks at you to see your description.


There is no auto line-wrap but you can line-wrap your description at the end by typing @f.
This will format your description with proper line-wrawpping. To leave editing mode, type:
@f and then @q

Follow these steps to write a description using the editor:
1. Type desc
2. Type your text.
3. Type @f (to format text)
4. Type @q (to quit)
5. Type look <name>
If you wish to make changes, continue to step 6:
6. Type desc
7. Type @c (to clear all the text)
8. Go to Step 2.

A description is required by level 10.

This is a role play command - use it to enhance your character!

See: help role play

entries.title: DIE
entries.keywords: die revive death dying debt resurrect
entries.body:
DIE
Author: Command Master
Keywords: die revive death dying debt resurrect


Type: Command


The die command brings you back to life!

If you have been killed in combat, you may die and return to life. You will be revived at
your religion's temple, or the center of Spur if there is no temple.

Note: If Quest Mode is on, your revive location is the current room.

entries.title: EMOTE
entries.body:
EMOTE
Author: Command Master
Keywords: emote 
Type: Command

Syntax: emote <message> - displays the message to the room, with your name first.


Emote displays a message to the room for role play purposes. Your name is highlighted in
yellow and quoted speech is highlighted in green. You can use $c to insert your capitalized
name.

Example:
emote jumps up on the table
Would show up as:
Dayrinni jumps up on the table.

A message that opens with punctuation runs straight on from your name, so possessives and
asides read naturally. A message that does not already end in . ? or ! gets a period.
Example:
emote 's eyes narrow
Would show up as:
Dayrinni's eyes narrow.

You can insert your character's pronouns based on your sex: $e (he/she), $s (his/her), and
$m (him/her).
Example:
emote grins and cracks $s knuckles.
Would show up as (for a male character):
Dayrinni grins and cracks his knuckles.

Capitalized $E (he/she), $S (his/her), and $M (him/her) insert your target's pronouns
instead - the nearest player or NPC you name with @ before the token.
Example:
emote claps @john on the back as $E grins.
Would show up as (if John is male):
Dayrinni claps John on the back as he grins.

You can target players, NPCs, or objects using the @ prefix, which is replaced with the
target's name.
Example:
emote looks at @john and waves at @sword
Would show up as:


Dayrinni looks at John and waves at an iron sword.

Targets are searched in this order: players/NPCs in the room, inventory, equipment, then
room objects.

Punctuation after a target is kept, so you can write possessives and asides straight
through.
Example:
emote looks at @john's red eyes, then at @sword...
Would show up as:
Dayrinni looks at John's red eyes, then at an iron sword...

For precise targeting, use a prefix modifier:
@name - searches all (player/NPC, then inventory, equipment, room)
@self or @me - your own name, so a line can refer back to you
@p:name - player/NPC only
@i:name - inventory only (also supports slot: @i:2 for slot 2)
@e:name - equipment only
@r:name - room only (also supports slot: @r:3 for slot 3)

The Firians, also known as Fir Elves, are forest elves deeply connected to the natural
world. They possess a great love for nature and are renowned for their exceptional archery
skills. Athletic in build, Firians prefer wilderness and outdoor living over urban
environments, blending effectively into shadows and the forest canopy. They are gifted with
night vision, making them formidable in low-light conditions. Firians are known as superior
marksmen, wielding missile weapons with unmatched proficiency, particularly bows. Their
foresters gain additional skinning bonuses, reflecting their deep practical knowledge of
the wild. While physically weaker in melee combat compared to more combat-focused races,
their agility and ranged prowess more than compensate. Firians maintain friendly relations
with most races, particularly the Anthians, but harbor a strong hatred toward the Sanene,

Bows recieve a 50% damage bonus if used outside of melee range(2 units (10 feet)) of a
target. Advance or retreat before battle to do maximum damage.

Flerians are short, mildly furry, slightly built humanoids with long dexterous fingers who
live in communal underground societies called burrows. They are friendly, curious,
talkative, and often dramatic, with short attention spans and a light-hearted nature. Their
narrow, sharp features are complemented by large, round eyes that grant them exceptional

Known for their remarkable agility and dexterity, Flerians move almost continuously and are
notoriously difficult to restrain. They have a well-earned reputation for grabbing anything
that is not nailed down, which often creates conflicts in urban areas. Despite caring
little for material possessions, they are fiercely loyal to their burrow and close
companions. Members of this race appear quite similar to one another to outsiders, making

Frontacians are one of the oldest and most influential races in Aradath, having ruled the
greatest single Empire the world has ever seen. During the Second and Third Ages they built
magickal bridges that linked the realm, and their name translates to "Jeweled Ones" owing
to the three embedded jewel-like formations found on their foreheads and palms. Tall and
pale with white hair and eyes, Frontacians view themselves as elite politicians, thinkers,
and runemages with aspirations for renewed dominance.

The race possesses exceptional magical talent, legendary arcane creations, and the ability
to drain energy from others. However, Frontacians suffer from a genetic malady tied to the
Great Unmagick, requiring a weekly medication derived almost entirely from dragon essence.
Missing a single dose causes instability, and two missed doses risk fatality. Physically
fragile compared to martial races, they compensate with unmatched intellect, cunning, and


raw magical power. Frontacians exhibit considerable imperial pride and a cold, uncaring
demeanor toward those they consider lesser, though honesty holds significant cultural value
within their own society.

entries.title: GO-BLIN
entries.body:
GO-BLIN
Type: Race
Keywords: Go-blin
Genders: Male, Female, Non-Binary
Allowed Classes: Fighter, Cleric: Order of the Heart, Cleric: Order of the Sword, Cleric:
Order of the Hand, Bard, Thief, Barbarian, Forester, Rune Mage, Psion

Racial Abilities: None

Go-blins are small, wretched creatures that dwell in dark cave systems, organized into
tight-knit clans. Standing only three to four feet tall, they possess a distinctive warty
green hide covered in pulsating yellow warts, broken tusks, and filthy skin. Their
uniformly black eyes peer out from faces universally considered repulsive, featuring
mottled green or grey skin with various visible deformities.

These nocturnal beings are compulsive hoarders, accumulating refuse and items of
questionable value from raids and scavenging expeditions. Spitting serves as a common
greeting among their kind, and they actively avoid sunlight whenever possible. Go-blins are
punks and bullies by nature, sadistic when the balance is in their favor, yet cowardly when
facing genuine threats. They prey on weaker creatures but scatter when confronted by
superior force, valuing cowardice as a survival mechanism and disdaining those who stand
and fight needlessly.

To learn more about the Go-blin please visit the web page:
http://dragonsgatereborn.com/races/race-goblin.html

Go-blin-als are believed to be servants to Chaos, possibly created through the warped
experiments of the Chaos Lords. Scholars suggest they may be remnants of a formerly mighty


race, corrupted and twisted by dark magic into the ugly, mottled green creatures seen
today. Standing approximately three feet tall, these bipedal beings are typically filthy
and foul-tempered, dwelling in caves within tight-knit clans.

Nasty, violent, and full of mischief, Go-blin-als are bullies and punks who become sadistic
when they hold the advantage but turn cowardly when facing genuine threats. They avoid
sunlight and delight in harassing weaker creatures. Spitting at each other is a common form
of greeting among their kind. They speak with distinctive lisp-like patterns and an
underdeveloped grasp of Common.

Go-blin-als possess natural night vision, quickness, agility, and dexterity, though they
suffer from a troublemaker reputation, physical weakness, and communication barriers with
other races. Their chaotic alignment draws them primarily to the profession of Thief, with
rare individuals becoming Fighters, Barbarians, or Rune Mages.

Hithuals are stout humanoids hailing from Aerhauven within the Great Divide mountain range.


Known as some of the finest miners in the lands, they possess above-average strength and an
unshakeable resolve. Their culture centers around mining, craftsmanship, and a deep loyalty
to family and clan.

Fun-loving, brave, proud, and stubborn, Hithuals show equal enthusiasm for hard work and
hearty leisure. They form acquaintances readily but develop lasting bonds with outsiders
mainly through shared combat experiences. Beards are worn as symbols of skill and respect
by accomplished warriors of any gender. They possess a significant natural resistance to
magic, though this same resistance prevents them from becoming Rune Mages.

Hithuals distrust non-traditional methods such as magic, thievery, or charity, firmly
believing that worthwhile accomplishments require genuine effort. They are also renowned
for their remarkable tolerance for ale and their love of practical jokes.

Author: Command Master

Type: Command

ID

Appraise a piece of armor or a weapon you are carrying or wearing

Syntax: id <item> - Appraise the named item.


Syntax: id q on <item> - Quality selector (q is shorthand, on is optional).
Syntax: id magick on <item> - Detect whether an item carries a magickal aura ('mag'/'magic' also work).

The identify (id) command appraises an item you are carrying or wearing, giving you
an estimated newly-forged value, weight, and condition rather than its exact stats.

Identify covers four kinds of item:
  armor  - estimates a piece of armor's cost, weight, and repair state.
  weapon - estimates a weapon's cost, weight, and condition.
  gem    - estimates a gem's silver value.
  magick - detects whether an item carries a magickal aura (also 'mag' or 'magic').

All four kinds of appraisal are available. Accuracy improves with your
appraisal skill, Intelligence, Wisdom, and Perception.

Unlike inspect, identify gives an estimated value/quality appraisal rather than the

A Tempest Season there are several types of rare materials used for high leveled weapons,
armor and shields.

These materials are required to purchase gear upgrades in the Tralisia Merchant District.

1. Acquire a piece of ore: trace or chunk.


2. Go to the Iron Works and have a smith refine the pieces into ingots by using the BUY command.
3. Take the refined ingots to the desired store, weapon or armor, and purchase the item.

Tips for finding ore and ingots is as follows:
Levels 40-69: Orinsteel - Cave and Lake Walkers
Levels 70-100: Platinum - Basin Worms and Ragweed Beasts (best drop rate)
Levels 100: Titanium - Hydras
Levels 100+: Karnite - Dead Oak
Levels 100+: Miltanium - Completing the quest Protect Tralisia: Destroy the Dead Oak Terror Knight and fighting frostbit trolls, ice spiders, and frost wyverns
Levels 100+: Wind-metal and Lightning-metal - Tower of Windis and Lita and the Hall of Elements in the Merchant Distrct
Levels 100+: Frost-metal - Ice Prison and the Hall of Elements in the Merchant Distrct 

The city of Tralisia is always looking to improve their supply and processing of ore and
events occur to do just this so stay tuned!

Monitanians are large, scaled, upright-walking lizard-like beings supported by powerful
tails. Originating primarily from the Dismal Swamp, they remain mysterious about their
history, though historical records recognize them as among the world's bravest peoples.
They communicate through gestures, hisses, and grunts, and cannot speak the Common tongue
due to vocal limitations, though they are highly intelligent despite racial assumptions
otherwise.

Monitanians value honor and allegiance above all else. Friendships are forged through
battlefield experiences and endure permanently. They possess natural clawing and biting
attacks, thick scaled skin that provides inherent armor, and night vision capability. Known
for their exceptional strength and sturdy physiology, they prefer the heaviest armor
available and often become mercenaries for just causes.

entries.title: MUATANA-AL
entries.body:
MUATANA-AL
Type: Race
Keywords: Muatana-al
Genders: Male, Female, Non-Binary
Allowed Classes: Fighter, Thief, Barbarian, Rune Mage
Racial Tensions: San Elf
Racial Abilities: None

The origins of the Muatana-al remain shrouded in mystery. Some believe they were once
cursed nobility, while others claim the Chaos Lords created them as instruments of terror.
Primarily associated with the Isle of Muldavia, they dominate the San Elves and their
leader, the Muatana-al Lord of the Dernath Woods, has allegedly forged pacts with Dragons
and Wyverns.

Tall and gaunt, the Muatana-al possess unnaturally pale flesh that seems to glow faintly in
darkness, with luminous veins visible beneath the surface in hues of crimson, blue, green,
and violet. They are cold, calculating, and utterly without mercy — intelligent predators
and patient hunters capable of stalking prey for extended periods. Solitary by nature, they
form alliances only when mutually beneficial, having long since abandoned any semblance of
compassion or empathy.

The Muatana-al must regularly drain the life force of living creatures to sustain
themselves. Feeding requires physical contact, leaving victims weakened, aged, or
desiccated. Without feeding, a Muatana-al suffers progressive weakness and eventual death.
They are strictly nocturnal creatures — sunlight causes searing pain and prolonged exposure
is lethal. Their entire culture revolves around the cycle of night and day.

To learn more about the Muatana-al please visit the web page:
http://dragonsgatereborn.com/races/race-muatanaal.html

The Oog-ra are extremely large, hairy humanoids with sloping foreheads and protruding
brows. Their massive frames feature sunken eyes and heavy fur, making them among the most
physically imposing beings in the lands. According to legend, the Oog-ra originated from
the icy Northern Isles, specifically a remote mountain range near Crescent Lake, and their
origins allegedly trace back to the Lords of Chaos.

While possessing incredible strength, the Oog-ra are widely regarded as the least
intelligent race. They are ruled by instinct rather than intellect, and though they can be
violent, they lack malicious intent. Their simple nature makes them easily manipulated and
often exploited by other races. Historical records show the Frontacian Empire once debated
exterminating them, and later attempted selective breeding to increase their intelligence.
Oog-ras enjoy destruction, particularly loud activities like smashing things, and are most
commonly found serving as Fighters and Barbarians.

Psycians are graceful, human-like beings with immense telepathic power, considered the
wisest of all races. They display a calm, distant exterior that masks deep emotion and
possess natural psychic abilities allowing them to probe minds at close range. A unique
glow forms around the head when their psychic abilities are in use.

Descended from survivors of the Isle of Psycia, which was destroyed by the ancient
Frontacians roughly a thousand years ago, the Psycians originally served as a telepathic
communication network for the Frontacian Empire. They staged a covert rebellion by
spreading misinformation, and in retaliation, Frontacian mages destroyed their island and


hunted the survivors. A few Psycians escaped to rebuild in secret, and they maintain an
unbridled hatred for the Frontacians and seek to restore their lost homeland.

Psycians are calm, logical, patient, and loyal, preferring peaceful resolutions to
conflict. However, overexposure to uncontrolled minds can cause madness, requiring regular
doses of a madness cure. Near Frontacians, they display open loathing and a loss of their
characteristic restraint.

Type: Command

quest request <npc name> - requests the quest from the NPC and adds it to your journal.
quest info <npc name> - asks the NPC about their quest but does not take it. This will display the start text.
quest return <npc name> - turns in a completed quest to a NPC and receives any rewards.quest journal - lists a summary of your quests.
quest journal <progress|completed|turnedin|all> - lists a summary of the quests in the indicated state. Can abbreviate these, ie: quest j p to view quests in progress.

Questing in A Tempest Season is an exciting and rewarding activity to take part in. The
commands above are how you interact with NPCs and their quests.

First, one must request a quest from a NPC. NPCs who have quests show up with (Quest)
around their names.

Second, after receiving the quest, you must complete the objectives. These may involve
finding items, visiting certain NPCs or rooms, or simply slaying beasts!

Finally, once the quest is finished, return to the original NPC to receive your reward!


You may also view your journal by typing 'quest journal'.

Some quests are difficult to solve - so feel free to ask for help. There are also rare
quests that give rich rewards so be on the look out!

picking up, unlocking or selling hordes of items.

The delays tick down every second and any commands entered which also are delayed, will be
placed in the queue. Not all commands are delayed actions, and can be performed while in
delay. Commands like say, inventory, and skills are examples for non-delayed commands.

The Sanene, also known as San Elves, are dark-skinned elves originating from the Isle of
Muldavia. Scholars theorize they are creations of Chaos rather than true elven descendants,
a distinction that sets them apart from other elven races. Shorter and more sinewy than
their Fir and Usil counterparts, the Sanene possess skin tones ranging from light golden to
deep dark brown, with predominantly black hair and dark eyes.

The Sanene prize power above all else: power of magick, weapons, information, and
manipulation. They are conniving, power-hungry, and quick to anger, embracing destruction
and death if it serves their purpose. Their alignment is fundamentally entropic and
chaotic, with a deep devotion to Chaos itself. Sanene often infiltrate positions of
influence within temples, governments, and elite circles, using their exceptional
intelligence and cunning to further their ambitions.

Among their advantages, the Sanene possess night vision, excellence in both weaponry and
magic, above-average strength for elves, and high intelligence. However, their inherently
untrustworthy and self-serving nature is their greatest hindrance, making lasting alliances
rare and tenuous.

entries.body:
SMOTE
Author: Command Master
Keywords: smote 
Type: Command

Syntax: smote <message> - displays the message to the room, where your name must be contained somewhere inside the message text.


Smote works like emote, except your name is not printed first automatically. Instead, you
provide your name (case insensitive) in the text. If your name is not provided an error
message is displayed. This does text highlighting for your name(yellow) and says (green).
You can also use $n and $c for auto replacement for your name. $n will not capitalize your
name, $c will. Note: All player names are already capitalized.

You can also use $n and $c for auto replacement for your name. $n will not capitalize your


name, $c will. Note: All player names are already capitalized.

You can insert your character's pronouns based on your sex: $e (he/she), $s (his/her), and
$m (him/her).
Example:
smote Dayrinni cracks $s knuckles as $e grins.
Would show up as (for a male character):
Dayrinni cracks his knuckles as he grins.

Capitalized $E (he/she), $S (his/her), and $M (him/her) insert your target's pronouns
instead - the nearest player or NPC you name with @ before the token.

Example:
smote You see Dayrinni look at you for a moment, before he says "Hello!"
or
smote You see $n look at you for a moment, before he says "Hello!"

You can target players, NPCs, or objects using the @ prefix. The @ prefix will
automatically be replaced with the target's name.
Example:
smote Dayrinni looks at @john and waves at @sword
Would show up as:
Dayrinni looks at John and waves at iron sword.

Objects are searched in this order: inventory, equipment, then room. Players and NPCs must
be in the same room.

Punctuation after a target is kept, so you can write possessives and asides straight
through.
Example:
smote Dayrinni looks at @john's red eyes, then at @sword...
Would show up as:
Dayrinni looks at John's red eyes, then at an iron sword...

For precise targeting, you can use prefix modifiers:
@name - searches all (player/NPC, then inventory, equipment, room)
@self or @me - your own name, so a line can refer back to you
@p:name - player/NPC only
@i:name - inventory only (also supports slot: @i:2 for slot 2)
@e:name - equipment only
@r:name - room only (also supports slot: @r:3 for slot 3)

Allowed Classes: Fighter, Thief, Barbarian, Rune Mage
Racial Tensions: They form their own opinions of each race as they play
Racial Abilities: None

Thugians are massive, brutish humanoids renowned for their exceptional physical power and
remarkable ability to survive. Considered among the strongest of all humanoid races, these
towering beings combine tremendous muscle with an almost supernatural capacity for rapid
healing, recovering from wounds that would fell lesser creatures. Their intelligence,
however, is severely limited, and their communication skills are poor at best.

Despite their fearsome reputation, Thugians have simple needs. They are almost constantly
hungry and will consume whatever is readily available, including the flesh of other
sentient beings, with particular fondness for humans and trolls. They are easily
entertained and attracted to small, shiny, or cute objects, becoming fiercely possessive of
anything that catches their eye. A well-fed Thugian can become a surprisingly loyal
companion, though their chaotic nature and unpredictable temperament make their anger
difficult to foresee. Preferred professions include Fighter and Barbarian, while Thief and
Rune Mage are exceedingly rare among their kind.

To learn more about the Thugian please visit the web page:
http://dragonsgatereborn.com/races/race-thugian.html

entries.title: TRAIN
entries.body:
TRAIN
Author: Command Master
Keywords: train trainer guildlist classlist raise
Type: Command

Syntax: train list - lists the abilities and specializations that can be trained at this location.
Syntax: train <slot> - trains the ability up to the next level. This will require a tier point and sometimes an item (the train will inform you on what is needed).
Syntax: train spec <slot> - trains the specialization up to the next level. This may require a tier point and a small fee.

Syntax: train tier cost - checks the cost of the next tier point you may buy.
Syntax: train tier buy - buys a tier point for the associated gold price.
Syntax: train tier respec confirm - resets all of your tier points for 5,000 gold. All of the abilities and specializations you trained will be set to lv 1. You will receive a 75% refund of your ability points.

Syntax: train guildlist - views your standing in your classes guild.
Syntax: train history - views your training attribute gain history.


The train command raises a level of an ability, specialization, or aptitude to the next
level.

The cost of raising to the next level varies:
1. Possibly using a TIER POINT and/or money, if applicable to raise an ability in level.
2. Using a TIER point (and money, if applicable) to raise a specialization in level.


The money cost to raise an ability up a level depends on the amount of uses the ability has
left.

You gain tier points upon leveling up.

You can also buy tier points at the trainer using 'train tier buy'.

Respeccing your tier points will set all of your non-natural abilities to their initial
level.

To learn more about training and learning new abilities visit the manual:
www.tempestseason.com/manual/abilities/#Training_Abilities_and_Specializations

entries.title: USILIN
entries.body:
USILIN
Type: Race
Keywords: Usilin
Genders: Male, Female, Non-Binary
Allowed Classes: Fighter, Cleric: Order of the Heart, Cleric: Order of the Sword, Cleric:
Order of the Hand, Bard, Thief, Rune Mage, Psion
Racial Tensions: They form their own opinions of each race as they play
Racial Abilities: None

The Usilin, also known as the Usil Elves, are widely regarded as the most intelligent race
in Eihydia. Devoted to scholastic pursuits and magical mastery, the Usilin prioritize the
accumulation of knowledge and self-improvement as central cultural values. They distinguish
themselves from other elven races through their unwavering focus on arcane research,
intellectual discourse, and the preservation of ancient lore.

Slender in build with pale complexions and refined elven features, the Usilin carry
themselves with a quiet confidence born of deep learning. Their society revolves around the
renowned Usilin Academy, a center of education and culture where the brightest minds gather
to study the arcane arts. While their exceptional intelligence and natural magical aptitude
make them formidable spellcasters, the Usilin are physically weaker than most races and
possess limited recovery capabilities.

The Usilin follow entropic alignment tendencies and practice diverse religious traditions,
with worship spanning deities such as Taath, Rinanni, Set, Sa, and Elindale. Common
professions among the Usilin include Cleric and Runemage, though some pursue the path of
the Bard. Fighters, Thieves, and Psions are rare among their kind.

To learn more about the Usilin please visit the web page:
http://dragonsgatereborn.com/races/race-usilin.html


See: help <ability name>, help <class name>, help races

The wield command tries to equip a weapon in the primary or secondary slot.

A weapon is needed to perform any melee attacks and to parry. Some skills may also require
an equipped weapon.

Some weapons can be swapped between 1 hand and 2 hand. To do this, use the grip command.

than fully fledged 2 handed weapons.


Not all classes can dual wield.

entries.title: WMOTE
entries.body:
WMOTE
Author: Command Master
Keywords: wmote arrival
Type: Command

Syntax: wmote enter <string> - switches to a new enter emote.
Syntax: wmote exit <string> - switches to a new exit emote.
Syntax: wmote current - views the current wmotes.
Syntax: wmote clear - resets your current wmotes to be default (nothing).


Wmote allows a player to change their enter and exit messages while moving between rooms
from the default enter and exit messsages.

Instead of seeing the default messages:
Dayrinni leaves southeast.
Dayrinni enters from the north.

Custom messages can be displayed, such as:
Dayrinni leaves southeast, while skipping.
Dayrinni enters, talking to everyone he sees from the west.

This is a role play command - use it to enhance your character!

This command will be monitored for abuse. Report anything inappropriate, including OOC
messages or anything that violates the game policy.
